A 64-year-old man presents with complaints of urinary dribbling and frequency. His medical history
includes hypertension and dyslipidemia. Physical examination reveals a 1-centimeter firm nodule on
prostate gland during digital rectal examination. His prostate-specific antigen level is 6.0 (reference
range upper limit: 4.0). The test has a sensitivity of 80% and specificity of 90%. A recent large
cross-sectional study (n=1000) demonstrated that prostate cancer prevalence in this age group is 10%.
What is the most accurate estimate of this patient's probability of having prostate carcinoma? Answer
Choices: (A) 8.9% (B) 63.2% (C) 15.3% (D) 31.6% (E) 47% (F) 80% (G) 72% (H) 10% (I) 90% (J)
44.4%
